definition_en: Used as the subject of a verb when addressing one or more people directly, regardless of formality or number in Modern English.

definition_en: A liquid or gel that contains ions and can conduct electricity, often used in batteries and biological systems.
example_en: The battery contains an electrolyte that allows current to flow.

definition_en: Describing a process or device that involves or is produced by electrolysis, the chemical decomposition of a substance using an electric current.
example_en: The electrolytic cell is used to separate water into hydrogen and oxygen.

definition_en: A device consisting of a coil of wire wrapped around a ferromagnetic core, which becomes magnetized when an electric current passes through the coil and loses its magnetism when the current stops.
example_en: Electromagnets are used in cranes to lift heavy metal objects.

definition_en: Concerned with or producing an electric current, typically through a difference in electrical potential.
example_en: The electromotive force in the circuit was measured in volts.

definition_en: A measure of the tendency of an atom or a functional group to attract electrons when forming a chemical bond.
example_en: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of all elements.

definition_en: The movement of charged particles suspended in a fluid under the influence of an electric field; positively charged particles migrate toward the cathode and negatively charged particles toward the anode.
example_en: Electrophoresis is used to separate DNA fragments by size.

definition_en: A scientific instrument used to detect the presence and sign of an electric charge, typically by observing the divergence of two thin metal leaves due to electrostatic repulsion.
example_en: The physics teacher used an electroscope to demonstrate static electricity.

definition_en: Concerned with, producing, or caused by static electric charges that are not moving.
example_en: Electrostatic discharge can damage sensitive electronic components.

definition_en: The branch of physics that deals with the study of stationary electric charges, electric fields, and the forces between them.
example_en: Electrostatics explains why a balloon sticks to a wall after being rubbed.

definition_en: The therapeutic use of electrical energy to treat medical conditions, such as muscle paralysis, pain, or nerve disorders.
example_en: Electrotherapy is often used to help patients recover muscle function after a stroke.

definition_en: Relating to or characteristic of an elegy; mournful or melancholy in tone.
example_en: The poem had an elegiac quality, mourning the loss of youth.

definition_en: A poem or song written in sorrow for someone who has died.
example_en: The poet composed an elegy for his late friend.

definition_en: Abnormal swelling and enlargement of body parts, especially the legs and scrotum, typically resulting from filariasis or other obstructions of the lymphatic system.
example_en: Elephantiasis causes severe swelling in the legs.

definition_en: Resembling an elephant in appearance, characteristics, or attributes.
example_en: The sculpture had elephantine ears and a long trunk.

definition_en: To deliberately leave out or strike out a part of something, such as a sound, syllable, or word.
example_en: In rapid speech, speakers often elide certain vowels.

definition_en: The omission of a sound or syllable in speech, often to make pronunciation easier or faster.
example_en: In rapid speech, 'going to' often undergoes elision to 'gonna'.

definition_en: The attitude or belief that a select group of people, often considered superior in intellect, wealth, or status, should have the most power and influence in society.
example_en: The politician was accused of elitism for ignoring the needs of the working class.

definition_en: A regular oval shape, traced by a point moving in a plane so that the sum of its distances from two fixed points (foci) is constant.
example_en: The orbit of the Earth around the Sun is an ellipse.

definition_en: Having the form or characteristics of an ellipsoid, which is a three-dimensional oval shape.
example_en: The planet has an ellipsoid shape due to its rotation.

definition_en: To make something longer in length or duration.
example_en: The artist elongated the figure in the painting for dramatic effect.

definition_en: To make something clear or explain it in detail.
example_en: The professor elucidated the complex theory for the students.

definition_en: The act of making something clear or explaining it in detail.
example_en: The professor's elucidation of the theory helped all the students understand it.

definition_en: Characteristic of or resembling an elf, especially in appearance or behavior.
example_en: The forest had an elvish quality, with shimmering lights and ancient trees.

definition_en: To free someone from slavery, servitude, or oppressive control.
example_en: The proclamation emancipated thousands of slaves.

definition_en: To treat a dead body with chemicals to prevent decay, especially for burial or display.
example_en: The ancient Egyptians embalmed their pharaohs as mummies.

definition_en: A professional who treats and preserves deceased bodies using chemicals and techniques to delay decomposition, typically for burial or viewing.
example_en: The embalmer carefully prepared the body for the funeral service.

definition_en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass or surface.
example_en: The archaeologist found a fossil embedded in the rock.

definition_en: An extra detail added to a story or account to make it more interesting, often not entirely true.
example_en: His story was full of embellishments about his adventures.

definition_en: To fraudulently take money or property entrusted to one's care, typically by an employer or organization.
example_en: The accountant was caught embezzling company funds.

definition_en: Serving as a symbol or representation of a particular quality, concept, or thing.
example_en: The dove is emblematic of peace.

definition_en: The opening of a wind instrument into which the player blows air to produce sound.
example_en: The flutist adjusted her embouchure before playing the high notes.

definition_en: A recess in a wall or parapet for a gun or cannon, often with an opening for firing.
example_en: Soldiers positioned the cannon in the embrasure.

definition_en: A person who decorates fabric with needle and thread, creating patterns or designs.
example_en: The embroiderer spent hours perfecting the floral pattern on the dress.

definition_en: To involve someone deeply in an argument, conflict, or difficult situation.
example_en: He was embroiled in a bitter legal dispute with his neighbor.

definition_en: The scientific study of how organisms form and develop before birth (or before hatching).
example_en: Embryology helps us understand how a single cell becomes a complex organism.

definition_en: Used to describe a professor, official, or professional who has retired but keeps their title as an honor.
example_en: Professor Smith is now professor emeritus of history.

definition_en: The reflex act of ejecting the contents of the stomach through the mouth.
example_en: The patient experienced severe emesis after the surgery.

definition_en: A drug or agent that causes vomiting, used to treat poisoning or for medical procedures.
example_en: The doctor administered an emetic to the patient who had ingested poison.

definition_en: A person who leaves their own country to settle permanently in another.
example_en: The emigrant left Ireland for America in search of work.

definition_en: The territory or domain that is ruled by an emir, often a small state in the Middle East.
example_en: The United Arab Emirates is a federation of seven emirates.

definition_en: The ideal refractive state of the eye where light rays focus precisely on the retina, resulting in clear vision without corrective lenses.
example_en: The optometrist confirmed that the patient had emmetropia and did not need glasses.

definition_en: A sequence of keyboard characters used to represent a facial expression, such as a smile or frown, in electronic communication.
example_en: She ended her message with a smiley emoticon like :)

definition_en: In a way that relies on observation, experiment, or experience rather than theory or pure logic.
example_en: The hypothesis was tested empirically through controlled experiments.

definition_en: The theory that all knowledge originates from sensory experience, rejecting innate ideas or revelation as sources of truth.
example_en: Empiricism argues that the mind is a blank slate at birth.

definition_en: A person who believes that knowledge comes primarily from sensory experience and observation, rather than from innate ideas or pure reason.
example_en: John Locke was a famous empiricist who argued that the mind is a blank slate.

definition_en: Having the necessary skills, qualifications, and physical or mental ability to be hired for a job.
example_en: The training program made her more employable in the tech industry.

definition_en: A medical condition characterized by the accumulation of pus in a body cavity, most commonly the pleural space surrounding the lungs.
example_en: The patient was diagnosed with empyema after the chest X-ray showed fluid buildup.

definition_en: A person who copies or tries to equal the actions, words, or achievements of another.
example_en: He is an emulator of his favorite artist, trying to paint in the same style.

definition_en: A substance that helps mix two liquids that normally do not combine, like oil and water, by reducing surface tension.
example_en: Lecithin is a common emulsifier used in chocolate production.

definition_en: To combine two liquids that do not normally mix, such as oil and water, into a stable mixture called an emulsion.
example_en: The chef used a blender to emulsify the oil and vinegar for the dressing.

definition_en: A mixture of two or more liquids that are normally immiscible, where one liquid contains a dispersion of the other.
example_en: Mayonnaise is an emulsion of oil and egg yolk.

definition_en: The act of performing or representing a story, event, or role.
example_en: The enactment of the historical battle was very realistic.

definition_en: One of a pair of molecules that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other, like left and right hands.
example_en: The two enantiomers of the drug had different effects on the body.

definition_en: A type of synovial joint where the rounded head of one bone fits into a cup-shaped socket of another bone, allowing free movement in multiple directions.
example_en: The hip is a classic example of an enarthrosis.

definition_en: To enclose or contain something in a small, protective casing or container.
example_en: The pharmacist encapsulated the medicine in a gelatin capsule.

definition_en: A rare congenital condition where brain tissue protrudes through an opening in the skull.
example_en: The infant was diagnosed with encephalocele shortly after birth.

definition_en: A graphical record of the electrical activity of the brain, produced by an electroencephalograph.
example_en: The doctor reviewed the encephalogram to check for abnormal brain activity.

definition_en: The part of the central nervous system contained within the skull, responsible for higher nervous functions and continuous with the spinal cord.
example_en: The encephalon is protected by the skull and meninges.

definition_en: Any disease or disorder that affects the structure or function of the brain.
example_en: The patient was diagnosed with a rare form of encephalopathy.

definition_en: In a way that is extremely attractive, charming, or delightful.
example_en: She smiled enchantingly at the audience.

definition_en: A distinct area or group that is surrounded by a different territory or culture.
example_en: The city has a small Italian enclave where the community maintains its traditions.

definition_en: To convert information, data, or a message into a specific code or format for transmission, storage, or security.
example_en: The software encodes the video file into a compressed format.

definition_en: The process of converting data or information into a specific code format for storage, transmission, or processing.
example_en: The encoding of the video file took several minutes.

definition_en: A formal expression of high praise or tribute, often in a speech or written work.
example_en: The professor delivered a heartfelt encomium for the retiring dean.

definition_en: To include a wide range of things or ideas; to cover entirely.
example_en: The course encompasses both theory and practical applications.

definition_en: To gradually intrude on someone's rights, property, or personal space.
example_en: The new building encroaches on our property line.

definition_en: The act of gradually taking away someone else's rights, land, or privileges.
example_en: The encroachment of the city into the countryside is a growing concern.

definition_en: To convert ordinary language or data into a coded form to prevent unauthorized access.
example_en: The software encrypts all user passwords before storing them.

definition_en: To make it difficult for someone or something to move or function by adding a heavy load or obstacle.
example_en: The hikers were encumbered by their heavy backpacks.

definition_en: A formal letter written by the Pope to all Roman Catholic bishops, addressing matters of doctrine, morals, or discipline.
example_en: The Pope issued an encyclical on climate change and social justice.

definition_en: Covering a wide range of subjects or topics; very thorough and extensive.
example_en: She has an encyclopedic knowledge of ancient history.

definition_en: A plant with crisp, bitter leaves, often used in salads or cooked as a vegetable.
example_en: She added chopped endive to the salad for a bitter crunch.

definition_en: A serious medical condition characterized by inflammation of the endocardium, the inner lining of the heart chambers and valves.
example_en: The patient was diagnosed with bacterial endocarditis after a prolonged fever.

definition_en: The thin, smooth membrane that lines the inside of the heart chambers and covers the heart valves.
example_en: The endocardium provides a smooth surface for blood flow within the heart.

definition_en: The tough, often woody or stony inner layer of the pericarp (fruit wall) that surrounds and protects the seed in certain fruits, such as peaches, plums, and olives.
example_en: The endocarp of a peach is the hard pit you discard.

definition_en: Of or belonging to endocrine glands or their secretions, which release hormones directly into the bloodstream.
example_en: The endocrine system regulates growth and metabolism.

definition_en: A doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating disorders of the endocrine system, which includes glands that produce hormones.
example_en: The endocrinologist helped manage her diabetes.

definition_en: The branch of medicine that studies the endocrine system, which includes glands that produce hormones and their effects on the body.
example_en: She decided to specialize in endocrinology after medical school.

definition_en: The innermost of the three primary germ layers in an embryo, which develops into the lining of the digestive tract, respiratory system, and associated organs.
example_en: The endoderm gives rise to the epithelial lining of the stomach and intestines.

definition_en: The practice of marrying only within one's own social, cultural, or ethnic group, often required by custom or law.
example_en: Endogamy was strictly observed in the royal family to preserve the bloodline.

definition_en: Produced or growing from within an organism, tissue, or cell.
example_en: Endogenous hormones are produced naturally by the body.

definition_en: Pertaining to the inner lining of the uterus, known as the endometrium.
example_en: Endometrial tissue can sometimes grow outside the uterus, causing endometriosis.

definition_en: A condition where tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, often causing pain and menstrual difficulties.
example_en: She was diagnosed with endometriosis after years of severe pelvic pain.

definition_en: A medical condition characterized by inflammation of the endometrium, the inner lining of the uterus.
example_en: The patient was diagnosed with endometritis after experiencing pelvic pain and fever.

definition_en: The mucous membrane that lines the interior of the uterus; it thickens under the influence of hormones and is shed during menstruation if no pregnancy occurs, or is expelled with the placenta after childbirth.
example_en: The endometrium thickens each month to prepare for a possible pregnancy.

definition_en: A neurochemical produced naturally in the brain that reduces pain and can create feelings of well-being or euphoria.
example_en: Exercise triggers the release of endorphins, which can improve your mood.

definition_en: A long, slender, flexible or rigid instrument used to examine the inside of a body cavity or organ, often equipped with a light and camera.
example_en: The surgeon used an endoscope to examine the patient's stomach.

definition_en: Of or relating to endoscopy, a medical procedure that uses an endoscope to examine the interior of a body cavity or organ.
example_en: The patient underwent an endoscopic examination of the stomach.

definition_en: A medical procedure that involves inserting an endoscope into the body to visually inspect the interior of a hollow organ or cavity.
example_en: The doctor recommended an endoscopy to examine her stomach lining.

definition_en: The tissue that surrounds and nourishes the embryo in the seeds of flowering plants, often rich in starch, oils, and proteins.
example_en: The endosperm provides essential nutrients for the developing plant embryo.

definition_en: Of or relating to the endothelium, which is the thin layer of cells lining the interior surface of blood vessels and lymphatic vessels.
example_en: Endothelial cells play a crucial role in regulating blood pressure.

definition_en: Describes a chemical reaction or process that absorbs heat from its surroundings.
example_en: Photosynthesis is an endothermic process that requires sunlight.

definition_en: A toxin that is confined inside the microorganisms and is released only when the microorganisms are broken down or die.
example_en: Endotoxins are released when Gram-negative bacteria undergo cell lysis.

definition_en: To naturally possess or be given a particular quality, ability, or characteristic.
example_en: She is endowed with great musical talent.

definition_en: In a manner that shows or requires great physical or mental energy; actively and enthusiastically.
example_en: She energetically cleaned the entire house before the guests arrived.

definition_en: To cause someone to feel drained of energy or vitality; to weaken.
example_en: The long, hot summer days enervated the workers.

definition_en: Describes a person who has the ability to speak and understand the English language.
example_en: The company is looking for English-speaking employees.

definition_en: The state of being swollen or congested with fluid, especially blood.
example_en: Breast engorgement is common after childbirth.

definition_en: So interesting or engaging that it takes all your attention.
example_en: The novel was so engrossing that I read it in one sitting.

definition_en: The continuation of a sentence or clause from one line of poetry to the next without a syntactical break or pause.
example_en: The poet used enjambment to create a sense of urgency in the stanza.

definition_en: To make something more lively, exciting, or interesting.
example_en: The colorful decorations enlivened the dull room.

definition_en: A feeling of weariness and dissatisfaction caused by lack of interest or excitement.
example_en: He suffered from a deep sense of ennui after retiring.

definition_en: An organic compound that contains a hydroxyl group bonded to a carbon atom which in turn is doubly bonded to another carbon atom.
example_en: The enol form of the molecule is stabilized by hydrogen bonding.

definition_en: The quality or state of being extremely large in size, extent, or number.
example_en: The enormousness of the task overwhelmed the team.

definition_en: To cause someone to become very angry or furious.
example_en: The unfair decision enraged the entire team.

definition_en: A person who has officially signed up for a class, course, program, or membership.
example_en: Each enrollee received a welcome packet on the first day.

definition_en: The act of officially registering or signing up for a course, program, or membership.
example_en: Enrolment for the autumn semester begins in August.

definition_en: To store and preserve green fodder (such as grass or corn) in a silo for use as animal feed.
example_en: Farmers ensile the corn crop to feed livestock during winter.

definition_en: To catch or trap an animal or person in a snare or net.
example_en: The hunter ensnared a rabbit in the forest.

definition_en: In Aristotelian philosophy, the state of a thing that has fully realized its potential; actual existence as opposed to mere potentiality.
example_en: The acorn’s entelechy is the fully grown oak tree.

definition_en: A friendly understanding or informal agreement between two or more nations, often for mutual benefit.
example_en: The two nations signed an entente to cooperate on trade.

definition_en: Of or relating to the intestines, especially the small intestine.
example_en: The patient was diagnosed with an enteric infection.

definition_en: Inflammation of the intestine, particularly the small intestine, often resulting in diarrhea and abdominal discomfort.
example_en: The patient was diagnosed with acute enteritis after experiencing severe diarrhea.

definition_en: A hard mass or calculus that forms in the intestines, often composed of mineral salts or other substances.
example_en: The patient was diagnosed with an enterolith causing a partial bowel obstruction.

definition_en: A thermodynamic quantity equal to the internal energy of a system plus the product of its volume and pressure.
example_en: The change in enthalpy is measured during the chemical reaction.

definition_en: To formally place a monarch or religious leader on a throne during a ceremony.
example_en: The archbishop enthroned the new king in a grand ceremony.

definition_en: The formal ceremony or act of placing a monarch, bishop, or other high-ranking figure on a throne, marking the beginning of their reign or office.
example_en: The enthronement of the new king was a grand event attended by dignitaries from around the world.

definition_en: To cause someone to feel excitement or strong interest in something.
example_en: The teacher's passion for history enthused her students.

definition_en: To give a particular title or name to a book, film, or other work.
example_en: The author entitled his novel 'The Silent Echo'.

definition_en: To place a dead body in a tomb or grave.
example_en: The pharaoh was entombed in a grand pyramid.

definition_en: Of or pertaining to the scientific study of insects and their relationships with the environment.
example_en: The entomological research focused on the behavior of bees.

definition_en: The branch of zoology that deals with the scientific study of insects.
example_en: She decided to specialize in entomology after her biology degree.

definition_en: An earnest, humble, or emotional request or plea.
example_en: She made an entreaty for him to stay.

definition_en: To surround a position with a trench, especially for military defense.
example_en: The soldiers entrenched themselves on the hill.

definition_en: The act of digging a trench or building a defensive position, especially in warfare.
example_en: The soldiers began the entrenchment of their position before dawn.

definition_en: A low-ceilinged floor located between the ground floor and the first floor of a building, often used for storage or as a mezzanine.
example_en: The apartment had a small entresol that served as a study.

definition_en: To twist or wind two or more things around each other.
example_en: The vines entwined around the old oak tree.

definition_en: To mention or count items one by one in a systematic way.
example_en: The report enumerates the main causes of the problem.

definition_en: The act of listing items one by one, or a list of items.
example_en: The report includes an enumeration of all the resources used.

definition_en: The act of pronouncing words or parts of words clearly and distinctly.
example_en: The teacher emphasized the importance of clear enunciation.

definition_en: To surround or cover something completely, often in a protective or enclosing manner.
example_en: The thick fog enveloped the entire city.

definition_en: In a way that is likely to be desired or admired by others, often due to good fortune or quality.
example_en: She is enviably talented at playing the piano.

definition_en: In a way that shows a feeling of jealousy or resentment towards someone else's advantages or possessions.
example_en: She looked enviously at her friend's new car.

definition_en: To form a circle around something; to enclose or surround on all sides.
example_en: The high walls environ the ancient castle.

definition_en: The theory that a person's environment, rather than heredity, is the primary factor influencing intellectual and behavioral development.
example_en: The psychologist's research was rooted in environmentalism, emphasizing the role of upbringing.

definition_en: To imagine or expect something to happen in the future.
example_en: The architect envisages a modern building with glass walls.

definition_en: Of, relating to, or produced by an enzyme; involving the action of a biological catalyst.
example_en: The enzymatic reaction was accelerated by the presence of a cofactor.

definition_en: The branch of biochemistry that focuses on the chemical properties, mechanisms, and biological functions of enzymes.
example_en: Enzymology is essential for understanding metabolic pathways.

definition_en: The most extensive division of geological time, spanning hundreds of millions of years.
example_en: The Precambrian eon covers the earliest history of Earth.

definition_en: A type of white blood cell that is easily stained by eosin dye and plays a role in allergic reactions and fighting parasites.
example_en: An elevated eosinophil count may indicate an allergic reaction.

definition_en: A bishop or metropolitan who is the head of an eparchy (a diocese) in the Eastern Christian tradition.
example_en: The eparch presided over the council of clergy in his region.

definition_en: A territorial division of ancient Greece, often corresponding to a region under a specific governor or administrative system.
example_en: The eparchy of Achaea was known for its cultural contributions.

definition_en: The addition of a vowel or consonant into the middle of a word to make it easier to pronounce.
example_en: In some dialects, epenthesis adds a vowel to break up consonant clusters.

definition_en: A white, odorless, powdered or crystalline alkaloid derived from plants of the genus Ephedra or produced synthetically, used to relieve bronchial congestion and treat asthma.
example_en: The doctor prescribed ephedrine to help open his airways during an asthma attack.

definition_en: A table or data set providing the calculated positions of celestial bodies (such as planets, stars, and moons) at specific times, typically published annually.
example_en: The astronomer consulted the ephemeris to predict the next solar eclipse.

definition_en: A vertical fold of skin that covers the inner corner of the eye, commonly found in people of East Asian descent and sometimes associated with certain medical conditions.
example_en: The epicanthus is a normal anatomical feature in many populations.

definition_en: A person who has both male and female reproductive organs or ambiguous sexual characteristics, making it impossible to assign a singular sex at birth.
example_en: The ancient Greeks sometimes considered hermaphrodites and epicenes as divine beings.

definition_en: The point on the Earth's surface that is directly above the underground origin (focus) of an earthquake.
example_en: The earthquake's epicentre was located near the coast.

definition_en: Relating to or characterized by the pursuit of pleasure, especially in food, drink, and comfort.
example_en: He led an epicurean lifestyle, always seeking the finest cuisine.

definition_en: A school of thought from ancient Greece that advocates seeking modest, sustainable pleasure as the highest good, often through friendship, knowledge, and simple living.
example_en: Epicureanism teaches that the absence of pain and fear is the greatest pleasure.

definition_en: A circle that rolls around the inside or outside of another fixed circle, generating a curve known as an epicycloid or hypocycloid.
example_en: The path traced by a point on an epicycle is a complex curve.

definition_en: A curve traced by a point on the circumference of a circle as it rolls externally along the circumference of another fixed circle.
example_en: The mathematician plotted an epicycloid to study its properties.

definition_en: Pertaining to the branch of medicine that deals with the incidence, distribution, and control of diseases in populations.
example_en: The epidemiologic study tracked the spread of the virus across the region.

definition_en: Concerning the study and analysis of the distribution, patterns, and determinants of health and disease conditions in populations.
example_en: The epidemiological study revealed a link between diet and heart disease.

definition_en: A scientist who investigates the causes, spread, and control of diseases within populations, especially epidemics.
example_en: The epidemiologist tracked the source of the outbreak to a contaminated water supply.

definition_en: The branch of medical science that studies the distribution, causes, and control of diseases in populations.
example_en: Epidemiology helps track how infectious diseases spread through communities.

definition_en: The outermost layer of the skin, providing a protective barrier against the environment.
example_en: The epidermis is the first line of defense against pathogens.

definition_en: A highly coiled tube located at the back of each testicle that stores, matures, and transports sperm cells to the vas deferens.
example_en: The epididymis is essential for sperm maturation.

definition_en: A medical condition characterized by painful swelling and inflammation of the epididymis, the coiled tube at the back of the testicle.
example_en: He was diagnosed with epididymitis after complaining of scrotal pain.

definition_en: Pertaining to the region of the abdomen located above the stomach and between the ribs.
example_en: The patient reported epigastric pain after eating.

definition_en: The part of the upper abdomen located just below the sternum, overlying the stomach.
example_en: The patient reported a sharp pain in the epigastrium after eating.

definition_en: A flap of cartilage located at the root of the tongue, which covers the opening of the windpipe during swallowing to prevent food or liquid from entering the airway.
example_en: The epiglottis automatically closes when you swallow to protect your lungs.

definition_en: A short quotation or saying at the beginning of a book, chapter, or other piece of writing, intended to suggest its theme.
example_en: The novel began with an epigraph from Shakespeare.

definition_en: The academic discipline that involves the study, interpretation, and analysis of inscriptions from ancient times, often carved on stone, metal, or other durable materials.
example_en: Epigraphy helps historians understand ancient languages and cultures.

definition_en: A secondary phenomenon that occurs alongside and as a result of a primary phenomenon, without having a causal influence on it.
example_en: In psychology, some argue that consciousness is an epiphenomenon of brain activity.

definition_en: A plant that grows on another plant for physical support, obtaining moisture and nutrients from the air, rain, and debris around it, without being parasitic.
example_en: Orchids are a common type of epiphyte found in tropical rainforests.

definition_en: Of or relating to a bishop or the system of church government by bishops.
example_en: The episcopal authority was challenged by the reformers.

definition_en: A surgical cut made in the perineum (the area between the vagina and anus) to enlarge the vaginal opening during delivery, helping to prevent severe tearing and facilitate the birth of the baby.
example_en: The doctor performed an episiotomy to assist with the difficult delivery.

definition_en: Relating to writing or narration that is composed of separate, distinct episodes or sections.
example_en: The novel has an episodic structure, with each chapter telling a different story.

definition_en: Bleeding from the nose, often caused by dry air, injury, or medical conditions.
example_en: The patient was treated for epistaxis after a minor fall.

definition_en: The set of ideas, beliefs, and intellectual frameworks that define what is considered certain knowledge in a particular era or culture.
example_en: The episteme of the Renaissance differed greatly from that of the Middle Ages.

definition_en: Of or relating to knowledge, its nature, limits, and validity; pertaining to epistemology.
example_en: The philosopher's argument was purely epistemic, focusing on how we come to know facts.

definition_en: Pertaining to the branch of philosophy that investigates the nature, origin, and limits of human knowledge.
example_en: The philosopher's epistemological arguments challenged traditional views of certainty.

definition_en: A person who studies or specializes in the theory of knowledge, especially with regard to its methods, validity, and scope.
example_en: The epistemologist presented a new theory about the limits of human understanding.

definition_en: The branch of philosophy that studies the nature, sources, and limits of knowledge.
example_en: Her dissertation focused on the epistemology of scientific discovery.

definition_en: Written in the form of or carried on by letters or correspondence.
example_en: The novel is written in an epistolary style, using letters between characters.

definition_en: A poem, song, or speech composed and performed in honor of a bride and groom during a wedding ceremony.
example_en: The poet recited a beautiful epithalamium at the royal wedding.

definition_en: Pertaining to the thin layer of tissue that covers the surfaces of organs, cavities, and structures throughout the body.
example_en: Epithelial cells line the inside of the mouth and stomach.
